rule.text: A duplicate invoice is detected by comparing each invoice against invoices received in the last 18 months for the same supplier using a normalised invoice number. [1] The system normalises the invoice number by removing spaces, slashes, hyphens, leading zeros, and trailing suffixes /A, /R, or -REV before comparison. [1] Two invoices are flagged as suspected duplicates when the supplier GSTIN and normalised invoice number match, or when the supplier, invoice date, and total amount (within ₹1) match. [1] Suspected duplicates are routed to the exception queue with code DUP_SUSPECT and are blocked from posting until a Senior Processor clears them. [1]

citations.quote: Before indexing, every invoice is compared with invoices received in the last 18 months for the same supplier. The comparison uses a normalised invoice number: remove spaces, slashes, hyphens and leading zeros, and drop a trailing suffix of /A, /R or -REV.

rule.text: The supplier's highest aggregate annual turnover of ₹6.5 crore exceeds the ₹5 crore threshold, so e-invoicing with an IRN is mandatory. [1] Because the invoice lacks an IRN, it is not valid for input tax credit and must be returned to the supplier with exception code IRN_MISSING. [1] The base value of the invoice must not be paid; a valid e-invoice will follow. [1]

citations.quote: A supplier whose aggregate annual turnover (AATO) in any financial year since 2017-18 has exceeded ₹5 crore must issue an e-invoice with an Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and QR code.

card.decision: Not acceptable — return for an e-invoice; pay nothing, including the base value

expert_tip.text: Invoices received Friday to Sunday are held until Tuesday noon to allow Infra GRN batching to complete.
expert_tip.author: Lakshmi

citation.quote: Infra sites batch their GRNs on Monday morning, so anything that comes in Friday to Sunday, I wait until Tuesday noon.
